fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled input bytes are admitted to MQTT v5 parsing; the 16-byte PoC (30 0e 00 00 0b 09 00 08 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00) is a PUBLISH packet whose remaining-length field consumes the whole input, so the parsed datagram ends exactly at the heap-buffer end.
dgram.len becomes 16 == input size, so end = dgram.buf + dgram.len is one byte past the heap allocation; any read at that address is a heap-buffer-overflow.

For the PUBLISH packet props_start = 5 and props_size = 11 are taken from the input (property length varint 0x0b, BINARY_DATA property id 0x09 with 2-byte length 0x0008); the properties section ends exactly at dgram.len.
Property iteration starts with ofs = 0; each call's return value becomes the next ofs.

The read pointer is computed from attacker-controlled props_start and ofs; after the first BINARY_DATA property, new_pos = 0 + 3 + val.len(8) = 11, so the second call has props_start(5) + ofs(11) == dgram.len(16), i.e. i == end.
end delimits the valid datagram region; the guard at line 211 mis-compares ofs (not props_start + ofs) against dgram.len, so it cannot reject the out-of-range pointer.

The 1-byte read of the property identifier executes unconditionally BEFORE the bounds check on line 211; the safety condition that should hold first is msg->props_start + ofs < msg->dgram.len (i < end).

First call parses the BINARY_DATA property: prop->val.len = 8 is taken from the two input bytes, so new_pos = ofs(0) + 1 + 2 + 8 = 11 == props_size; the returned ofs is fed to the next call, placing i exactly at end.

Second call with ofs = 11: i == end == dgram.buf + dgram.len, one byte past the 16-byte heap buffer; the dereference i[0] performs the heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in mg_mqtt_next_prop (ASan top frame, called from fuzz.c:68).
